title: Etale monomorphisms of algebraic spaces are open immersions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $f$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], tested on scheme charts, and is a monomorphism of sheaves: for every $S$-scheme $T$, the map $X(T)\to Y(T)$ is injective. Then $f$ is an open immersion, meaning that every scheme base change is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: Fix any $S$-scheme $T$ and morphism $y:h_T\to Y$. The sheaf fibre product $E=X\times_Yh_T$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $g:E\to h_T$ be its projection. Interpret the chartwise etale hypothesis as in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]: for every representable etale scheme chart $U\to X$, every scheme base change of $U\to Y$ is an etale scheme morphism. This is the representable-etale condition on that composite, not on $f$. The base-change clause of that node makes $g$ chartwise etale. No representability of $f$ or $g$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 05W5 (lemma-etale-universally-injective-open), scheme-base-change reduction, specialized to a monomorphism.

proof.text: For every $S$-scheme $H$, the set $E(H)$ consists of pairs $(x,t)\in X(H)\times h_T(H)$ with $f_H(x)=y_H(t)$ in $Y(H)$. If two pairs have the same $t$, injectivity of $X(H)\to Y(H)$ makes their $x$ entries equal. Thus $g$ is a monomorphism. In $E(H)\times_{h_T(H)}E(H)$ the two entries are consequently equal. The diagonal $E\to E\times_{h_T}E$ therefore has inverse the first projection, naturally in $H$. For a scheme test $h_H\to E\times_{h_T}E$, pull back this inverse: the pullback of the diagonal is isomorphic over $h_H$ to $h_H$ itself, so is represented by $H$ with its identity map. This is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]: the whole target is closed in itself and the identity sheaf map is surjective. This verifies separatedness in the exact scheme-test form needed below.

source.place: Tags 042M (lemma-monomorphism), 042N (lemma-monomorphism-separated), and lemma-base-change-monomorphism; the pair and diagonal arguments are written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite] to the chartwise etale map $g:E\to T$. It is chartwise locally quasi-finite. Step 2 gives its diagonal as a closed immersion on every scheme test. The two hypotheses of [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] now hold, so there is a scheme $Z$ over $T$ and an isomorphism $h_Z\cong E$ over $h_T$. This does not require $E$, $T$, or $g$ to be quasi-compact or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 05W5 (lemma-etale-universally-injective-open), representability paragraph; Tag 03XU (lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite) and Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme).

proof.text: Identify $E$ with $h_Z$ by the isomorphism of step 3, and write $p:Z\to T$ for $g$. The scheme-source equivalence in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] makes $p$ an etale scheme morphism; equivalently test its chartwise property on $\operatorname{id}_Z$. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. It is a monomorphism of schemes: if $a,b:H\to Z$ satisfy $pa=pb$, this common composite gives $H$ its $S$-structure, both maps are $S$-morphisms, and the injectivity proved in step 2 gives $a=b$. Hence [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open] applies to $p$ and proves that it is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 025G (theorem-etale-radicial-open), implication (3) implies (1), the final scheme step of Tag 05W5; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03FR (definition-etale), agreement for scheme morphisms.

proof.text: The open immersion $p:Z\to T$ represents the sheaf projection $X\times_Yh_T\to h_T$ from step 1. Since $T\to Y$ was arbitrary, every scheme base change of $f$ is represented by an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. This is exactly the asserted open-immersion condition on $f$.
